author: Michael Larabel
description: In addition to the surprising impact of /proc/filesystems read optimizations for Linux 7.2, another one of the VFS pull requests for this next kernel version is delivering some nice improvements for EXT4 and XFS around IOmap, the framework that maps file data offsets in memory to their physical locations on storage...
title: Linux 7.2 Optimization Shows +5% IOPS For EXT4 & XFS After Moving Around Two Lines Of Code

author: Michael Larabel
description: After some last minute delays pushing the 15.1-RELEASE back by two weeks, FreeBSD 15.1 is now shipping as the newest stable release of this BSD operating system...
title: FreeBSD 15.1 Released With Updated WiFi Drivers, Better C23 Support & Other Improvements

author: Michael Larabel
description: The community of developers continuing to maintain Ubuntu Touch for smartphones has released the Ubuntu Touch 24.04-2.0 beta ahead of the planned stable release in mid-July...
title: Ubuntu Touch 24.04-2.0 Beta Now Properly Handles Notches & Rounded Corners

author: Michael Larabel
description: The newest open-source project out of Intel is the Intel Performance Skills project that is providing AI agent skills to help with CPU performance analysis and performance optimizations on Linux...
title: Intel Performance Skills: New Open-Source Project Leveraging AI For Linux Performance Optimizations

author: Michael Larabel
description: The FreeBSD Project announced today the launch of an AI-Assisted Vulnerability Discovery Project with grant funding provided by the Linux Foundation backed Alpha-Omega project. Alpha-Mega has sponsors including Microsoft, AWS, Google, Anthrophic, OpenAI, and others who will now be helping with FreeBSD uncovering new vulnerabilities by leveraging AI...
title: FreeBSD Receives Funding To Launch AI-Assisted Vulnerability Discovery

author: Michael Larabel
description: Last month a new GCC back-end was proposed for WebAssembly to allow C/C++ code to be compiled to WASM with this GNU compiler toolchain. The GCC Steering Committee has evaluated it and approves the notion of WebAssembly back-end for GCC...
title: GCC Steering Committee Supports Inclusion Of WebAssembly Backend

author: Michael Larabel
description: After days of dealing with 1,500+ packages in the Arch Linux AUR containing malware, the latest headache in the Arch Linux User Repository is Russian spam and offensive messages...
title: Russian Spam & Profanities Are Now Plaguing The Arch Linux AUR

author: Michael Larabel
description: The Firefox 152.0 release binaries are now available ahead of tomorrow's official unveiling. With Firefox 152 there is now the JPEG-XL support code being compiled by default for the release albeit still disabled at run-time by default behind a preference for now...
title: Firefox 152 Now Available With JPEG-XL Support Built By Default, Modernized Settings UI

author: Michael Larabel
description: Reading /proc/filesystems for obtaining a list of file-systems supported by the running kernel is done frequently on Linux. Namely due to being read by the SELinux library (libselinux), reading of /proc/filesystems is done more often than one would typically expect and now the Linux 7.2 kernel is optimizing for it to yield much better performance...
title: Reading /proc/filesystems Is Surprisingly Done Very Often & Now As Much As 444% Faster

author: Michael Larabel
description: The scheduler updates were merged this morning for the Linux 7.2 kernel and it's exciting. Cache Aware Scheduling has finally been merged! This is a win for especially modern Intel and AMD processors with multiple last level caches (LLCs)...
title: Cache Aware Scheduling Merged For Linux 7.2 For Boosting Modern Intel & AMD CPUs

author: Michael Larabel
description: Miguel Ojeda already mailed in the many Rust code changes for the in-development Linux 7.2 kernel. This is quite a big Rust code with more than forty thousand new lines of Rust code in the kernel...
title: Linux 7.2 Introducing The Rust Zerocopy Library To Eliminate More "Unsafe" Code

author: Michael Larabel
description: Newly-merged code for the in-development Linux 7.2 kernel will now expose the case-folding (case insensitive) behavior of local file-systems so that Linux file servers and others can properly report the actual behavior rather than guessing if case-folding is actually used/supported...
title: Linux 7.2 To Better Communicate File-System Casefolding For Helping Windows NFS & More

author: Michael Larabel
description: Following yesterday's release of the upstream Linux 7.1 kernel release, GNU Linux-libre 7.1 is out with its new build for de-blobbing various drivers from loading non-free-software microcode/firmware and other sanitizing of the kernel code in the name of software freedom...
title: GNU Linux-libre 7.1-gnu Released With More Driver Deblobbing, Unhappy With i486 Removal
